newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil private coffee sector to meet again Aug 28.
newsitem.headline: Brazil private coffee sector to meet again Aug 28.

text.p: Private sector representatives of Brazil's coffee council, the CDPC, will continue talks on issues affecting the sector on August 28, a producer official said after a meeting today.

Officials from the producing, exporting, domestic roasting and soluble coffee industries met in Belo Horizonte today and discussed "how to improve the relationship between the different segments," said Rui Queiroz who had called the meeting.
Queiroz is president of the coffee committee at the National Agriculture Confederation (CNA).
The CDPC comprises six members each from the public and private sectors together with its president, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles.
It was set up this year with much ceremony but its last full meeting with the minister took place in May and a date hate the proposal and so far no decision has been reached.
Against this background, today's meeting was called to discuss ways to add impetus to the council, traders said.

"The goal is not to overshadow the CDPC but in the same way that government officials meet to prepare for the CDPC, the private sector is doing the same thing so that it can decide on its agenda and what it needs," one trader said.
Today's meeting focused on general issues affecting the sector without going into specifics, Queiroz said.
The August 28 meeting will be held at 1000 local/1300 GMT at the Sao Paulo headquarters of the National Coffee Council.
